key_insight: A-site high-entropy disorder and tensile strain jointly improve oxygen evolution activity in nickelate thin films, while the high-entropy material better resists degradation than LaNiO3.
engineering_relevance: The study offers a materials-design strategy for perovskite oxide electrocatalysts for water electrolysis, not solar cells or AI.
method: Study epitaxial (La0.2Pr0.2Nd0.2Sm0.2Eu0.2)NiO3 films under different strain conditions.
Probe structural defects, Ni valence, and electronic states using characterization including O K-edge X-ray absorption.
Combine first-principles calculations with OER activity and degradation comparisons.
evidence_signal: Tensile-strained films show earlier OER onset, stronger pre-catalytic Ni redox features, and higher activity than compressively strained films and representative single-A-site nickelates; the abstract reports no numerical performance metrics.
watch_item: Practical scalability and long-duration operating stability remain unclear from the epitaxial thin-film results summarized in the abstract.
paper_title: High-Entropy A-Site Disorder Enhances Oxygen Evolution Reaction Activity and Stability in Nickelate Thin Films
